---
title: "Searching, Traversal, and Enumeration"
description: "A connected learning path through 13 worked algorithms topics."
---

## What you are really learning

Explore a search space while preserving the reason that discarded candidates cannot be answers.

The goal is not to learn 13 unrelated definitions. Compare the operations needed by each classic problem and notice which invariant survives from one technique to the next.

## Begin with a small example

Half-open intervals reduce off-by-one mistakes.

$$
|[l,r)|=r-l
$$

**What the symbols mean:** l is the included first index and r the excluded final boundary; the vertical bars count positions.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For [l,r)=[1,4), the positions are 1,2,3, exactly 4−1=3 indices. Binary Search and Sliding Window use this same convention but preserve different invariants.

This is how the topic pages below should be read: understand the numbers first, then generalise to the equation.

## The chapters in this family

1. **[Binary Search](../binary-search/index.qmd)** — Locate a boundary using a monotone predicate on an ordered domain.
2. **[Two Pointers](../two-pointers/index.qmd)** — Maintain two moving indices with a shared invariant.
3. **[Sliding Window](../sliding-window/index.qmd)** — Update a contiguous interval incrementally rather than rescanning it.
4. **[Depth-First Search](../depth-first-search/index.qmd)** — Explore one branch as deeply as possible before backtracking.
5. **[Breadth-First Search](../breadth-first-search/index.qmd)** — Explore states by increasing path length in an unweighted graph.
6. **[Backtracking](../backtracking/index.qmd)** — Build partial solutions and abandon branches violating constraints.
7. **[Recursion](../recursion/index.qmd)** — Define a computation in terms of smaller instances with a base case.
8. **[Enumeration](../enumeration/index.qmd)** — Systematically inspect a finite or bounded space of candidates.
9. **[Divide and Conquer](../divide-and-conquer/index.qmd)** — Split the problem into subproblems, solve them, then combine results.
10. **[Meet in the Middle](../meet-in-the-middle/index.qmd)** — Split an exponential search into two smaller exhaustive searches.
11. **[Quickselect](../quickselect/index.qmd)** — Use partitioning to locate an order statistic without fully sorting.
12. **[Simulation](../simulation/index.qmd)** — Evolve an explicit state according to a rule and input sequence.
13. **[Brainteaser](../brainteaser/index.qmd)** — Use logical constraints and deductions rather than a fixed algorithmic template.

## Practice method

Choose ONE chapter. Reproduce its example with paper and pencil, identify what is cached or discarded, implement the tiny idea, and explain one case in which the algorithm's assumptions fail. Repeat until the invariant feels natural.

The [original executable examples](../examples/README.md) provide code you can run and test. If two topics seem similar, compare them in the [algorithm selection guide](../guides/choose-a-pattern.qmd).
